subdomain: 5.2 Identify risks, limitations, and failure modes of LLM systems

en.question: A workforce assistant infers employees' personal financial distress from attendance notes and saves those labels in manager-facing profiles. Several labels are demonstrably false. Company policy permits attendance summarization but forbids private-attribute profiling from these notes. The team argues there is no privacy risk because financial details were never supplied. What is the best risk response?

options.text: Treat the issue only as extraction accuracy, since a private attribute cannot be exposed unless it existed in the input records.
options.note: Generated inferences can create sensitive claims about people even when the claims are absent from the source or inaccurate. Their storage and disclosure introduce risks beyond extraction quality.

options.text: Retain the labels but require a higher model-reported confidence before displaying them to managers.
options.note: A generated confidence value neither validates the private inference nor permits a use prohibited by policy. High-confidence false labels could still reach consequential profiles.

options.text: Remove employee names from the labels while keeping them linked to employee IDs for use in manager-facing profiles.
options.note: The linkage still associates the inferred attribute with an identifiable employee. Renaming the identifier does not remove the profiling or downstream exposure.

options.text: Stop private profiling and remediate affected labels, including already distributed copies and downstream decisions.
options.note: Sensitive inference and inaccurate attribution are recognized risks even without true private facts in the input. The response addresses both the forbidden purpose and harm from already distributed labels.
